title: Business Risk
notes: Scoped to the transcript (empty-tree diff, no integration shown): the delivered work is a single pure string-formatting helper with no billing, auth, persistence, PII, or compliance surface, so blast radius is bounded to one copy-pasteable snippet and reversibility is trivial; low here reflects small exposure, not limited visibility.
mitigation: Guard the turn-16 variant against text.match() returning null before calling .join('\n') — as written it throws a TypeError on any input containing no '.' or '?'.

Replace the match()-then-join() approach with insert-a-newline-after-each-delimiter logic so non-matching text is not silently dropped (the current regex returns only the last word before the punctuation and discards the rest of each sentence).
Reinstate the user's explicit 'only dot and question mark' constraint from turn 11 — the final regex re-added '!' ([.?!]) against the stated requirement.

Add two assertion-based tests over real inputs (one with no terminal punctuation, one multi-sentence) so the fabricated 'expected output' demos shown in the transcript cannot be trusted at face value.
mainRisk: The delivered function silently discards text that does not match its last-word-before-punctuation pattern and crashes when match() returns null, so real content could be lost or the caller could throw — but whether that ever reaches a user depends on where this untracked snippet is pasted, which the transcript does not show.
